rules: Assume experienced maintainers are skeptical of AI-assisted work: earn trust with small, conventional, reproducible, byte-matched contributions; avoid generated noise, speculative naming, and promotional AI language. Do not misrepresent authorship or required disclosure.

Expansion-first priority: enable new characters, scenes/events, maps, dialogue, sounds/music, and graphics through matching source, editable data, verified interfaces, and useful tools. Generic cleanup/input work is secondary unless it removes a concrete content-expansion obstacle. Keep new-content changes separate from the byte-perfect baseline.
Do not equate actor/NPC schedule locations with player scene transitions without call-path proof.
Do not name numeric map IDs from string proximity alone.
Prefer script-facing action/query paths and authoritative Location packing helpers.

Top priority: minimize guessing. Cross-check proposed gameplay interpretations against documented original GBA FOMT mechanics before semantic naming or publication; distinguish other versions and remakes.
Record consulted source URLs and specific supporting claims. Separate exact ROM/data-flow evidence, documented gameplay, and hypotheses; investigate disagreements and preserve uncertainty.
ROM equivalence verifies binary preservation, not semantic correctness. Online gameplay descriptions do not independently prove internal pointer provenance.
